newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia gives tenants two days to leave building.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia gives tenants two days to leave building.

text.p: Twenty-five families received a two-reprieve in their battle with the city to remain in a condemned apartment house, officials said late Saturday.

With temperatures heading below freezing, the License and Inspections Agency allowed the families to stay in Ogontz Manor in the Olney section despite 66 citations for unsafe living conditions. The agency had condemned the high-rise structure Monday and set a 5 p.m. Saturday deadline for leaving.

"We made a very good faith effort to keep this building open for tenants," said Fran Egan, L&I commissioner, "but unfortunately there were just too many violations," including deficiencies in electrical wiring and heating.
George Gould, a lawyer for the tenants, said city officials had betrayed the tenants and had not provided $2,000 relocation grants, as promised.

Two city councilmen charged that Mayor Ed Rendell had reneged on a promise to provide $500,000 to rehabilitate the building. Spokesmen for the mayor said the cost was too high for the number of housing units it would preserve.
The councilmen said they plan to hold a hearing on the issue Monday.
